The test image shows a tomato stem with:
- White/bleached mycelial growth on the stem
- Small dark spherical bodies (sclerotia) scattered on the white area
- Stem collapse/rotting at that point
- Another stem section on the right showing similar white coating

This pattern — white mycelium + small, round, dark sclerotia on the stem — is characteristic of Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*). Now viewing a reference image to confirm.

The reference confirms Southern Blight: white mycelial growth on the stem near the soil line. The test image matches perfectly — white bleached stem lesion with small dark sclerotia (the tiny mustard-seed-like black bodies), which is the hallmark sign of *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight).
